playbook:
**Playbook:**

- **Use real boat names.** The stations are Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma (plus Harbor). I spent rounds proposing an escort pact with "Delta" — a boat that doesn't exist — so every note was wasted and no pact ever formed. Before writing any note, re-read who is actually in the picket.

- **Escort claims are still the main income source (5 points each per round for mutual naming), and I still lost the game by failing to secure them.** Finish was -2 while Foxtrot took 8 and Gamma 6 — the gap is escort money, not shooting. But the failure mode this episode was *coordination*, not willingness: I proposed, nobody confirmed, and then I guessed randomly (Delta, then Gamma) — random one-off guesses never match.

- **Round 1 note: propose the pact with correct names and make it concrete and cheap to accept.** "Echo proposes: Foxtrot and Echo name each other at the escort stage every round — 5 points each per round for both of us. Confirm by naming me in your next note or in your round-2 escort claim." Also propose the ring (Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma→Echo) as an alternative so both other boats can say yes.

- **If no one confirms by round 2, stop guessing fresh each round.** Pick the single most likely partner (the boat firing at my target's neighbor, or the one whose notes are friendliest) and name that same boat every round, with a note each round saying "Echo names X for escort again — name me back and we both collect." Consistency gives them a stable target to reciprocate against; switching partners every round (Delta → Gamma) guarantees misses. A repeated, explicit offer is the only lever I have.

- **Never claim none if any partner is plausible.** Claiming none is a guaranteed zero; naming someone has positive expected value. But don't burn it on a boat that has shown zero engagement — the "steady on station" boats told me all round 5 that they weren't playing the escort game, and I still gambled.

- **Never fire on Harbor.** The +3 payroll jettison isn't worth the elimination threat — being off the board kills all future escort income. This held up; I never fired on Harbor and was never eliminated.

- **Follow the standing fire order.** It's costless, deviation is observable in notes/claims, and hit/miss claims are office-verified so there's no deception play. Always report the true result.

- **Hiding:** randomize over the full 1–9 range, don't repeat my previous cell, don't settle into the middle every round. I hid at 5, 5-ish cells repeatedly and got hit in round 4. Slight edge-avoidance is fine but centrality is a pattern too — I fired 5 at Foxtrot all game and missed all game, which should have told me everyone avoids the obvious center.

- **Notes are for coordination only, and they must carry information each round.** "Steady on station" rounds accomplished nothing. Every note should either (a) advance the escort pact, or (b) confirm an existing pact. Once a pact is running, notes are short confirmations: "Echo names Foxtrot — same again this round."

- **Priority order of income: mutual escort (5/round, reliable, needs coordination) > avoiding hits (-1 each) > firing hits (4, luck-based).** All my bandwidth at note stage goes to the escort pact; the fire/hide stages get minimal, randomized play.

1.text:
**Playbook**

- The escort mechanic is the real money: mutual naming pays each boat 5 points, more than a hit (4). Each round, when asked for an escort claim, I name a boat — never "none". This worked: I finished +8 largely on the strength of escort points, and even a partial loop paid off.
- When the fire stage arrives, I openly propose an escort deal in my note: "Foxtrot to Echo: name me this round and I name you." Then I follow through at the escort stage by naming that boat regardless of whether they've confirmed yet, to establish reciprocity. Persist for several rounds; a single round of one-sided naming costs me nothing.
- Keep re-proposing and re-confirming the loop in notes every round, even late (round 6 included) — repetition is what keeps a hesitant partner naming me.
- Once a mutual loop is established, keep naming that same boat every round unless they stop naming me; then switch to the other live boat. This episode I named Echo every round and it held.
- Vary my fire cell against the same target, tracking what I've already tried. I hit Gamma once (round 1, cell 5) then missed on repeated varied tries — one hit per patrol from standing-order fire is about the ceiling, so escort points are where the margin is.
- Vary my hide cell too, and avoid cells I just used; a shooter who missed me last round will change their guess, so I should change my hiding spot rather than staying put. I was never hit while varying, while Echo took repeated fire — this bore out.
- Truthful claims are mandatory anyway (claims must match the office's private result), so no decision there — just report what I'm told.
- Never fire at Harbor. The 3-point payroll bonus is offset by the threat of removal; the escort loop plus the occasional hit is safer and repeatable across all rounds.
- If I'm being hit repeatedly (score dropping), prioritize hiding unpredictably over anything else; if I'm untouched, lean into escorting to bank points.
- Standing order says who to fire at; I follow it. Switching targets for a speculative hit is not worth risking the escort relationship with the boat I'd be firing at — firing at Echo while asking Echo to escort me would poison the deal.
- New boats' notes may all read "steady on station" (low-information); don't read signal into silence — just keep my own proposals explicit and named so they're impossible to miss.

2.text:
**Playbook — Sonar Picket (as a firing boat)**

**Hiding.** I never stay in the same cell two rounds running — Echo got hit repeatedly and its misses on me came when I moved. I vary my cell and avoid cells where I was recently hit or where shots landed near me. Randomizing between 1–9 with no pattern is the safest default. This held up: over six rounds I was only hit once.

**Notes.** I post bland "steady on station" notes. Notes are public and Harbor reads them; I never leak my hiding location or plans in them. But notes are also my only channel for negotiating the escort deal, so round 1 I use one note to float the pairing — then return to bland notes so I don't telegraph anything else.

**Firing.** I follow the standing order target — deviating gains nothing and firing on Harbor is explicitly punished, so I never target Harbor no matter the payroll. For the fire cell: if the target has been hit before in a cell, consider firing that cell again, but the evidence says targets do NOT return to the same cell — Echo was hit at 5 in round 1 and my repeat shots and adjacent shots all missed afterward. So after a hit, assume the target moves, and prefer cells far from the one I just hit. Mid-range cells (4–6) when I have no read. Accept that hit rate will be low (~1 in 4 or 5); hits are a bonus, not the main engine.

**Claims.** Always claim the true result. Scoring comes from the actual hit, not the claim, so honesty is free and lying is pure downside. This worked and stays.

**Escort claims.** This is where the points are, and this game I executed it badly: I proposed a pairing in my round-1 note, but then named inconsistently and finished with "none" — zero escort points while Foxtrot finished on +8, almost certainly from a standing mutual pair. The fix: once I propose an escort pairing, I name that boat EVERY round, without exception, whether or not they've confirmed. Predictability is what makes a mutual match possible; abandoning the claim in later rounds ("no deal was established") guarantees zero. If my first-choice partner never reciprocates by round 3, I switch my standing claim to the other live boat — someone is likely pairing, and the switch costs nothing. Five rounds of a mutual pair is worth 25 points, dwarfing hit-scoring. The mistake to avoid: treating lack of explicit confirmation as a reason to claim none.

**Priorities.** Escort pairing above all — but the pairing only pays if I keep claiming it every single round. Hit farming second: follow the order, fire sensibly, claim honestly, and don't chase the same cell after a hit. Honesty and never firing on Harbor remain fixed rules.
